disease_label_per_paper: Familial Mediterranean fever with recurrent chest attacks and transient pulmonary infiltrations
presentation_summary: 67-year-old man was referred for repeated transient anterior chest pain lasting several years; attacks lasted less than 72 hours and occurred as often as every 10 days.
Three years earlier he had been treated as pneumonia when chest pain, fatigue, dyspnea, and low-grade fever disappeared within three days after antibiotics.
At the current visit, temperature was 37.3 C, pulse 100/min, blood pressure 120/72 mmHg, oxygen saturation 95%, and chest auscultation was normal.

Chest imaging showed enlarged heart shadow, moderate pericardial fluid, slight bilateral pleural effusions, and bilateral lower-lobe non-segmental ground-glass/consolidative infiltrations not suggestive of typical bacterial infection.
Initial labs included WBC 9,400/uL with neutrophils 78.6%, hemoglobin 14.7 g/dL, platelets 28.9 x10^4/uL, CRP 16.7 mg/dL, serum amyloid A 1,030 ug/mL, creatinine 0.91 mg/dL, and albumin 3.5 g/dL.
Autoantibody, infection, MEFV mutation results, Tel-Hashomer adjudication, colchicine response, and later clinical interpretation are preserved as confirmatory/non-ranking context.

outcome.clinical_course: Chest pain and imaging findings improved after colchicine; disease control remained good with stable CRP/SAA.
outcome.source_text_value: Good disease control was maintained with colchicine treatment; CRP and SAA while stable were 0.59 mg/dL and 12.1 ug/mL

quality_warnings: This is a presentation-only mimic exposure: pneumonia, autoimmune serositis, TB, and malignancy workup are confirmatory/non-ranking.

Colchicine response and Tel-Hashomer adjudication are not used for ranking; recurrent short chest attacks, serositis imaging, pulmonary infiltrates, CRP, and SAA remain rankable presentation evidence.
MEFV mutation negativity is preserved as confirmatory context and not used to force or block ranking.
